Poking around the internet during and after the debate, I noticed some things. On social media, especially Facebook (yes, I know, bad uvulectomy), the comments were flying fast and furious.

In nearly EVERY case, if the person was a Hillary supporter, the comments were along the lines of "what a whiny little bitch", "how can they let a presidential candidate talk that way?", and other disparaging comments about Trump. Not ONCE did they address any of the points he brought up. Not ONCE did they provide a better solution to any of his policies. Nothing said when Hillary spouted nonsense, when she deflected simple questions, or when she proved by her own words that she was lying about things she said just minutes before. Nope, all about "Trump is a whiny baby", "Trump is evil" etc.

In my opinion, Trump won if we're just tallying points. But they were both sloppy, deflected way too often, missed opportunities, and preferred playground bullshit to an actual debate. But while many of us can see the faults on both sides, the Hillary camp seems to only be able to spout simple statements with no real counter-point, to say nothing of rebuttal. If Trump had pressed her harder on things like what would happen with a no-fly zone in Syria and used her own words against her when she claimed to support the Second Amendment, it would have gone from a decent win to a slam-dunk, IMO. He scored major points with Saudi Arabia, Haiti, etc., but I think he could have pressed those points a little more to twist the knife a bit. He had her on the ropes with those.

I gotta hand it to Hillary. She knows her base (low-information, easily manipulated, smug, emotional voters), and she's pandering to it HARD with a disturbing amount of success. I just hope that, as much as I don't like Trump, his administration is the bitter pill we have to swallow for a chance at turning things around, rather than the cyanide capsule a Clinton administration would be.

Anyway, just my $0.02 with no real point other than to ramble a bit.
